newsitem.title: ITALY: Milan's Linate airport closed after milk protests.
newsitem.headline: Milan's Linate airport closed after milk protests.

text.p: Italian aviation authorities said on Friday they were closing Milan's Linate airport to air traffic for a week because of security reasons after protesting farmers blocked road access to it.

Dairy farmers set up blockades around northern Italy's busiest airport to protest against EU fines imposed on them for exceeding strict milk quotas. Farmers have also thrown up road blocks at Milan's second airport, Malpensa, and Venice airport.

The deputy director at Linate, Vincenzo Fusco, told Reuters the airport would be shut down from 1600 GMT on Friday until 1600 GMT on January 31. He added that the airport could be re-opened at any time if the blockade was lifted.
"The airport has been closed because access roads were blocked and in the event of any accident we would not have been able to organise a rescue operation," he said.
Italian dairy farmers have been hit with some 370 billion lire ($235 million) of fines, which have to be paid by the end of the month, for exceeding milk quotas.

They want the government to pay the levies and have camped out in Milan for nine days to press their case. The farmers closed access to the airports on Friday after Prime Minister Romano Prodi reiterated that the state would not pay the fines.
